Anthropic just filed to go public — and the ripple effects will reach every company with an AI strategy.

The S-1 filing landed on October 26, positioning Anthropic for one of the largest tech IPOs in recent memory. The same week, Meta moved to raise up to $95 billion for its own AI buildout. Capital is not just flowing into AI anymore. It is restructuring around it.

Here is why this matters if you run a business: when your AI vendor goes public, its economics become transparent. Pricing models, safety investments, governance frameworks, revenue concentration — all of it enters the public record. That is a gift for enterprise buyers, but only if you know how to use it.

The executives who treat this as background noise will find themselves locked into vendors that cannot sustain their pricing or their promises. The ones who pay attention will use this transparency to negotiate better terms, assess real risk, and build AI architectures that do not depend on a single provider's survival.

AI vendor selection just became a board-level financial decision, not a technical procurement exercise.
